 *J U D G M E N T*

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ on account of injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.

*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL*
 2.

Facts leading to the case of the petitioner forthcoming in the petition that, on 15.09.2013 at about 2.30 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding in a motor cycle,
bearing registration No.KA51V2964, as a pillion rider,
near Service road, HosurBengaluru NH7 road, Attibele check post, Anekal, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of  SCCH-18 3 MVC No. 2300/2020 the Lorry bearing registration No.TN29AX3038 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life.
Consequently, dashed against the motor cycle, in which the petitioner was proceeding.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to Sparsh Hospital, wherein, he was treated as an inpatient.
The petitioner had spent huge amount towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment.
4. It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 18 years, working as paper delivery boy and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
And he used to spend the said amount, for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to his severe injuries.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the rider of  SCCH-18 4 MVC No. 2300/2020 the offending vehicle bearing No. TN29AX3038.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Attibele Police as per Crime No.253/2013.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. After registration of the case, as usual notices were issued to the respondents.

In response to the notices,
the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court,

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 had appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement, in answer to the case of the petitioner.
7. In the objection of the respondent No.2, has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
But, seriously denied about the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further, admitted about the insurance  SCCH-18 5 MVC No. 2300/2020 policy and its validity.
It is the main contention of the respondent that, the accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA51V2964.
But, not on the part of the driver of the offending lorry bearing No.TN29AX3038.
It is another contention of the respondent that, the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving license to drive the said vehicle at the time of accident.
And stated that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and without any basis.

With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

On taking birds eye view towards the police papers, go to show that, alleged accident was occurred on 15.09.2013.

With respect to one day delay, in giving first information, the complainant Praveen H.R. narrated in the complaint marked at Ex.P2 and in the Ex.P1 column No.3(c), since he was providing treatment to the injured  SCCH-18 10 MVC No. 2300/2020 who, is none other than his brother, belated complaint was given.

19. On the basis of his information, criminal law set in motion against the rider of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.TN29AX3038 alleging that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.

In the recitals of Ex.P1 & Ex.P2, and in the spot mahazar executed by the investigation officer, as per Ex.P3, in the presence of complainant and panch witnesses, disclose that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver and also consequent upon the involvement of the vehicle, accident in question had taken place and the petitioner had sustained injuries in the said accident.

These three material documents remained Mr. Deepak H.N vs Sekar M on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51215540/

20. Added to this, on going through the wound certificate marked at Ex.P4, goes to show that, on the history of RTA, the petitioner had sustained two grievous injuries.
The history narrated with respect to the accident in the above documents, remained unshaken, as the other side not placed any rebuttal evidence to disprove the recitals of the said document.

21. Ultimately, on going through the final report submitted by the investigation officer as per Ex.P5, goes to show that, after due investigation process against the driver of the offending vehicle by name V.Keshavan S/o.
Venkateshan, said report has been submitted alleging that, he has committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

22 . It is pertinent to note that, the affidavit evidence and the documentary evidence placed by the petitioner, has not been challenged by the respondent by producing contra  SCCH-18 12 MVC No. 2300/2020 Mr. Deepak H.N vs Sekar M on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51215540/

But, to disprove the case of the petitioner,
about the direct nexes between the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, remained unshaken and uncontroverted, by placing cogent and convincing evidence, except production of authorization letter and insurance policy.

In such a situation, I am of the view that,
the evidence given by the petitioner is to be accepted.

Even at the time of crossexamination of PW1, though several questions put the witness, nothing worthwhile is elicited to shaken and to eradicate the evidence given by the PW1, in support of the above issue and also to prove the defenses of respondent company against the rider of the offending vehicle.

Even suggestions put to the PW.1, to the effect that, the rider and pillion rider were not worn helmet, as on the date of accident, and due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the two wheeler, accident had taken place,

Apart from this, with respect to the defence that, the rider of the two wheeler, while  SCCH-18 13 MVC No. 2300/2020 overtaking another vehicle, caused accident to the offending vehicle, had also, clearly denied by the PW.1 in toto.

 24.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of relief claimed by the petitioner.

The petitioner through this petition claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident,
under different heads.

25. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him, in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the Mr. Deepak H.N vs Sekar M on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51215540/

"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court  has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to  the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation  should not be assessed conservatively.

On the other hand,
 compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure  some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding  compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result  of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair  reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining  quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to  strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable  demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the  SCCH-18 15 MVC No. 2300/2020  opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That  sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes  in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is  made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding  adequate compensation. "
26. In connection with the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P4.

The said document discloses that, he sustained the following injuries:
 1. Fracture of left femur.
 2. Cut lacerated wound over left leg.
27. In connection with the above injuries, doctor opined that, the injury No.1 & 2 are grievous in nature.

Apart from this, the petitioner has produced discharge summaries, medical bills, prescriptions, advance receipts,
xray and 3 CT scan reports as per Ex.P7 to Ex.P13.

On Mr. Deepak H.N vs Sekar M on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51215540/

Bengaluru, as per Ex.P7 and Ex.P8 disclose that, the petitioner had taken the treatment as an inpatient from 15.09.2013 to 19.09.2013 and from 03.06.2015 to 18.09.2015.

For having taken the note of the nature of the  SCCH-18 16 MVC No. 2300/2020 injuries sustained by him, as fully narrated in Ex.P7, and mode of treatment taken by him and also by keeping in mind about his sufferings during the said period of treatment, in connection with the grievous injuries, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.50,000/ towards pain and suffering.
28. Another point to be discussed herein, about the loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
In the petition, he had stated that, he was working as paper delivery boy and earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
To substantiate the said fact, there is no iota of documents to show that, the petitioner was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
On the other hand, it is to be noted that, the injuries sustained by him, are grievous in nature, as per the wound certificate.

On going through the discharge summaries of Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru, as per Ex.P7 and 8 discloses that, the petitioner had taken the treatment as an inpatient from 15.09.2013 to 19.09.2013 and from 03.06.2015 to 18.09.2015.

Hence, definitely there was some difficulty to him, during the period of treatment and Mr. Deepak H.N vs Sekar M on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51215540/
13  SCCH-18 17 MVC No. 2300/2020 followup treatment, to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for one month.

Hence, I am of the view that, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,000/
towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

29. The petitioner herein, in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence, placed 5 medical bills of Rs.99,786/ as per Ex.P9 along with prescriptions as per Ex.P10, advance receipts as per Ex.P11.

At the time of crossexamination of PW1, except the suggestion that, the medical bills are created documents, nothing worthwhile is elicited to disbelieve the same and also no contra materials placed to impeach the said medical bills.

As such, by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and mode of treatment taken by him, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.99,786/
under the head of medical expenses.
30. The petitioner herein, as per the medical records, had sustained grievous injuries.

On going through  SCCH-18 18 MVC No. 2300/2020 the discharge summary of Sparsh Hospital the petitioner underwent wound debridment and suturing of left leg Mr. Deepak H.N vs Sekar M on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51215540/
14 wound and CRIF with IMIL nail left femur and had taken the treatment as an inpatient from 15.09.2013 to 19.09.2013 as per Ex.P7.
Further, as per Ex.P8 the discharge summary of Sparsh Hospital the petitioner underwent left femur removal on 04.06.2015 and was an inpatient from 03.06.2015 to 18.09.2015.
Later on, he was advised for further treatment.
As such, during the period of treatment, and further treatment, the petitioner could have spent some amount towards travelling, food and nourishment.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/ towards attendant charges,
food, and nourishment and conveyance charges.
31. Another material point of loss of future income is concerned, the petitioner herein, asserting that, he has sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate, along with other medical documents.
In the  SCCH-18 19 MVC No. 2300/2020 evidence of the PW1, reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.

As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him, as per Ex.P4, goes to show that,
the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
To substantiate this, the petitioner has placed, wound certificate and xray for consideration.

Apart from this, the petitioner had placed the evidence of the doctor by name Mr. Deepak H.N vs Sekar M on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51215540/
15 Dr. S.A.Somashekara as PW3.
 32.

In the evidence of this material witness, PW3,
deposed that, on the history of RTA, the petitioner had sustained injuries.

On 25.02.2022 when he was examined the petitioner, clinically and radiologically, in order to assess his disability, came to know that, on 15.09.2013,
he met with an accident, and sustained injuries of fracture shaft femur left.
In this regard, he underwent surgery of wound debridment and suturing of left leg wound and IMIL nailing process was done on 15.09.2013 and implants were removed on 14.06.2015.
Apart from this, PW.3 scrutinized the wound certificate and two discharge summaries, before assessing the disability.
33 . On examination he found walks with pain and limping, wasting of left lower limb and surgical scars are seen over left hip and thigh.
Secondary scars are seen over left proximal leg.
On the basis of xray he found united fracture shaft of femur.

After assessment of several aspects of his disability on the point of mobility components,
stability components, by giving additional points, came to the conclusion that, total disability of the left lower limb of the petitioner at 36% and whole body physical disability is at 18%.
In support of the evidence of PW3, had placed Ex.P15 and Ex.P16 for consideration.

16  34.
In support of the evidence of PW.3, placed OPD card and clinical examination report along with Xray as per Ex.P16.
At the time of crossexamination of PW.3 answered that, now the fractures are united, and he did not know documents in connection with further treatment of the petitioner.

Further, he admitted that, implants not yet removed, and further he assessed the disability with respect to mobility and stability components as well as with respect to the whole body disability to help the petitioner  SCCH-18 21 MVC No. 2300/2020 and he answered that, only in connection with physical disability, he expressed the opinion.

35. Overall appreciation of the evidence of PW.3,
along with the documentary evidence, the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, I am of the view that,
the percentage of disability, assessed by the PW3, seems little bit exorbitant.

Hence, by taking in to consideration of the age of the petitioner, and also, on the point that,
implants already removed, and in the absence of followup treatment documents, it is apt to take the percentage of disability as 10% instead of 18%, the same will meets the ends of justice.

36 . In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition Mr. Deepak H.N vs Sekar M on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51215540/
17 reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 25 years.
In support of the age proof, he has placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P6.
On going through the said documents, pertaining to the petitioner, the date of birth of  SCCH-18 22 MVC No. 2300/2020 the petitioner has been mentioned as 30.03.1996.
The accident occurred on 15.09.2013.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner is considered as 17 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '18' is to be taken into consideration.

37. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in the main petition, and also in the examinationinchief evidence, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, prior to the accident, he was working as paper delivery boy and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
In support of his avocation and definite income per month, he has not placed any iota of documents.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.

Hence, by keeping in mind about the year of the institution of this case, and also, as per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.8,000/ for the year 2013.

38. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner,
to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
 Rs.8,000 X 12 X 18 X 10/100= Rs.1,72,800/.

By taking into consideration of all these aspects, and also by taking in to consideration of the age of the petitioner, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.10,000/ towards loss of amenities.

 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Pain and Suffering 50,00000
2 . Loss of income during 8,00000  laidup period and rest  period  3.
Medical expenses 99,78600  4. Attendant, Nourishment 10,00000  and Conveyance Charges  5. Loss of future income 1,72,80000  6. Loss of Amenities 10,00000

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,50,586/(Rupees Three lakhs fifty thousand five hundred and eighty six only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in MFA No.103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. LIABILITY:
 43.
As regards the liability is concerned, in the case on hand, accident has not been seriously disputed by the other side.

And the evidence given by the petitioner that,
due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, Lorry bearing registration No.TN29 AX3038, remained unshaken.

The assertion of the Mr. Deepak H.N vs Sekar M on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51215540/
20 petitioner that, the insurance policy pertaining to the offending vehicle was in force as on the date of the accident,
has not been denied by the respondent No.2.
 44.
As per the records policy was valid from 31.12.2012 to 30.12.2013.
Accident was occurred on 15.09.2013.
The policy furnished by the respondent No.2 also speaks about the existence of policy of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident, as reflected in Ex.R2.
Further, the respondent No.2 has failed to prove that, due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, alleged accident had taken place.

Since as on the date of the  SCCH-18 26 MVC No. 2300/2020 accident, insurance policy was valid, both the respondents No.1 and 2, being the owner and the insurance company of the offending vehicle respectively, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
45 . However, the respondent No.2, being the insurance company and indemnifier has to satisfy the award.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2, is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

Accordingly,
I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
 46.
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

Consequently, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,50,586/ (Rupees Three lakhs fifty thousand five hundred and eighty six only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/.
Draw award accordingly.
